# 4 Ezra Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — Third dialogue

---

**1** He answered: The Most High made this world for many, but the world to come for few.

**2** I will give you another comparison, Ezra: ask the earth and it will tell you — it produces far more common clay for making pots than it does the rare dust that yields gold. That is the pattern of this present world.

**3** Many are created. Few will be saved.

**4** I said to myself: Soul, absorb what you have been told. Heart, take wisdom into yourself and hold it.

**5** You came into life without being asked. You will leave it against your will. You have been given very little time.

**6** O LORD above us, allow your servant to pray in your presence. Give us a seed to plant in our hearts, and the cultivation of understanding in our minds, so that it may bear fruit — the fruit by which every mortal made in your likeness will be able to live.

**7** For you alone truly exist. We are merely the work of your hands, as you yourself have said.

**8** You give life to the body taking shape in the womb, fitting it with its limbs. Your creation is held safe through fire and water, and for nine months your work sustains what is being formed inside.

**9** What holds and what is held are both kept safe by you. When the womb finally releases what was made inside it,

**10** you have arranged that from the body's own tissues — from the breasts — milk will be provided,

**11** so that what was shaped may be nourished for a season, and after that you guide it in your mercy.

**12** You nourished it in your righteousness and trained it in your law and corrected it in your wisdom.

**13** You will take it away in your death and make it live in your life.

**14** If therefore you are going to destroy one who was shaped with such effort at your command, what was the purpose of making him?

**15** Now I will speak: about all humanity you know best — but I want to speak about your people, who are the source of my grief,

**16** about your inheritance, for whom I mourn; about Israel, for whom I am in pain; about the seed of Jacob, who cause me constant anguish.

**17** Therefore I begin to pray before you on behalf of myself and of them, because I see so many of us who live here falling.

**18** And I have heard how swiftly the Judge approaches who is coming.

**19** So listen to my voice. Understand what I say. I am going to pray before you. [Here begins Ezra's prayer, spoken before he was taken up:]

**20** O LORD, you who live in eternity, whose eyes are raised above everything and look down from on high,

**21** whose throne is too vast for any thought to measure, whose glory surpasses all understanding, before whom the armies of angels stand and tremble,

**22** at whose word they become wind and fire: whose every word is reliable and whose every utterance stands, whose command is powerful and whose ordinance inspires awe,

**23** whose very glance drains the ocean depths, whose anger melts the mountains, and whose truth never ends:

**24** Hear, O LORD, the prayer of your servant. Take in the petition of your creature. Pay attention to what I say.

**25** As long as I breathe I will speak. As long as I can reason I will answer.

**26** Please — do not look at your people's sins. Look instead at those who served you honestly.

**27** Do not reckon the efforts of those who do evil. Reckon the efforts of those who kept your covenants through suffering.

**28** Don't think about those who lived wickedly before you. Remember those who chose, of their own free will, to honor and fear you.

**29** Do not desire to destroy those who lived no better than animals. Look at those who taught your law magnificently.

**30** Don't be angry at those who seem lower than beasts. Love those who have always relied on your justice and your glory.

**31** We and our ancestors have spent our lives on roads that lead to death. But it is precisely because of us sinners that you are called merciful.

**32** If you are willing to show mercy to us — people who have no record of righteous deeds — then you will fully deserve to be called the Merciful One.

**33** For the righteous, who have a rich account of good works stored with you, will receive their reward from their own deeds anyway.

**34** But what is a human being, that you should be angry with them? What is this dying race, that you should be so bitter toward it?

**35** The truth is, there is no one born on earth who has acted with complete integrity, and no one capable of understanding who has not sinned.

**36** This is exactly where your justice and goodness show up, O LORD: in showing mercy to those who have no treasury of righteousness.

**37** He answered: Some of what you have said is correct, and it will be as you said.

**38** But I myself will not concern myself with the creation of those who have sinned — not with their death, their judgment, or their end.

**39** What I will celebrate is the creation of the righteous, their journey through life, their salvation, and the reward they receive.

**40** As I have said, so it shall be.

**41** A farmer sows a lot of seeds in the ground and sets out many seedlings — but not all the seeds will sprout on schedule, and not all the seedlings will take root. In the same way, not everyone sown into the world will be saved.

**42** I said: If I may, I want to say something.

**43** The farmer's seed — if it doesn't germinate because your rain didn't come when it was needed, or if it was ruined by too much rain — that seed is lost. The same happens to a person fashioned by your hands, called your image, made to be like you — the one for whose sake you made everything — whom you compared to the farmer's seed.

**44** Please don't be angry with us. Spare your people. Have mercy on your inheritance. After all, you do have mercy on your own creation.

**45** He answered: What is present belongs to those who live now. What is to come belongs to those who will live then.

**46** You could not possibly love my creation more than I love it — but you have repeatedly compared yourself to the unrighteous.

**47** Don't do that. Even so, you will be worthy of praise before the Most High

**48** because you have been genuinely humble — as is right for you — and have not thought yourself deserving of high honor among the righteous.

**49** For many terrible things will come upon those who inhabit the world in the last times, because they walked in enormous pride.

**50** But look to yourself, and seek the kind of glory that belongs to people like you:

**51** because paradise has been opened for you, the tree of life has been planted, the time to come has been arranged, abundance has been provided, a city has been built, rest has been granted, goodness has been completed, and wisdom prepared in advance.

**52** The root of evil is sealed off from you. Weakness and decay are hidden from you. Corruption has vanished into oblivion.

**53** Sorrows have been left behind, and at the end the treasure of immortality will be unveiled.

**54** So stop asking about the multitude of those who perish.

**55** They had their chance to choose and they rejected the Most High, held his law in contempt, and walked away from his ways.

**56** They trampled on his righteous people.

**57** They told themselves there is no God — while knowing perfectly well that they would die.

**58** Just as the good things I described will receive you, so the thirst and torment prepared for the wicked will receive them — for the Most High never wanted human beings to perish.

**59** But the human being who was created defiled the name of his Maker and refused to be grateful to the one who gave him life.

**60** And so my judgment is now close.

**61** I have not told these things to everyone — only to you and a few like you. And I said:

**62** O LORD, you have shown me a great many signs that you will perform in the last days, but you have not told me when they will happen.
